policies.description: All required fields for the update_child_incident operation (child_incident_mapping_id, parent_incident, child_incident) must be provided and non‑empty before invoking the tool.
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.policy_name: Role‑Based Access for Updating Incident Relationships
policies.description: Only users with roles Administrator, Manager, or Agent may perform update_child_incident, as these roles have full CRUD permissions on incident‑related tables.
references: Administrator (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables.

Manager (manager) | Supervision, Escalation, Approvals | Full CRUD on operational tables (incident, problem, change, knowledge); READ access to all the tables. Can reassign incidents/requests. Can approve/reject Change Requests. Monitors SLAs and escalations.

Agent (agent) | Frontline Incident/Request fulfillment | Full CRUD on Incidents, Service Requests, Tasks, Work Notes, CMDB, Change, Problem, and Knowledge. READ access to all the tables. Can update assignment, state, and resolution. | Cannot bypass approvals, or change system administration settings.

policies.description: The update_child_incident must be executed as a single validated operation, not combined with other actions.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints.

policies.description: Do not fabricate or guess any identifiers (such as child_incident_mapping_id, parent_incident, child_incident). The tool must first verify that each ID exists via a confirmed lookup before performing the update.
references: Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results.

policies.description: Before updating a child‑incident mapping, ensure that the referenced parent and child incidents actually exist and that all required relationships are satisfied; otherwise the operation must be halted.
references: Referential Integrity: Before closing any record, verify that all mandatory dependencies are satisfied.

policies.description: If the invoking user’s role does not include the required CRUD permissions for incident relationship tables, the operation must be aborted and a 403 Forbidden response returned.
references: 403 Forbidden: Permission denied (user role lacks authority for the operation).

policies.description: Any request that breaches a defined policy (e.g., missing mandatory fields, insufficient role, failed referential integrity) must be stopped immediately, and the specific policy reason must be returned before any further action.
references: Policy Violation: If a user request violates any rule herein, you must halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.
